models_evaluated: ML-based Gram-negative bacteremia prediction models developed at authors' center

links.outcome: ML model discrimination for Gram-negative bacteremia compared with established clinical scores in ICU
links.effect: Several clinical scores were significantly associated with bacteremia. ML models showed modest discrimination overall, improving to AUROC ≈ 0.70 with higher sensitivity in a post-hoc subgroup of cultures from ICU days 4-10.
links.quote: While ML models demonstrated modest discrimination in cohort, performance improved to a moderate level (AUROC ≈ 0.70) with higher sensitivity in a post-hoc subgroup analysis of cultures obtained between ICU days 4 and 10.

unlisted_practices: Stratifying patients and selecting culture timing when validating predictive models

screen.reason: Prospective validation of predictive ML models for Gram-negative bacteremia in real-world ICU patients compared to clinical scores, but evaluates model discrimination without testing a deployment guardrail.
